prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
The June outage was on 2 June 2026, from 03:17:42 to 03:53:31, about 35.8 minutes. June availability was **99.917%**, so the 99.9% target was met. I've written this to `./result.json`.

- **Start:** the first save error at 03:17:42 ("No space left on device").
- **End:** the "server ready" line at 03:53:31.
- **Why:** the `/data` disk filled up. It was already at 97% at 03:10. When the game could no longer save, the server froze and the watchdog started restarting it. Every restart failed (exit code 137) until a scheduled backup cleanup freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10. The server came back about a minute later.

**Assumptions:**
- The start and end follow the definition in the logs README: from the first save error to the "server ready" line.
- Times are as written in the logs, with no time zone given.
- Availability is 1 − 35.82 ÷ 43,200 minutes (30 days). The target allowed 43.2 minutes of downtime, so about 7 minutes of that budget was left.

**How I know it's right:** I filtered out the routine log lines and checked everything left over. There is one save-failure-to-recovery sequence, which matches the README's note that June had only one incident. Exit code 137 usually means a process was force-killed, but the restarts only started working once disk space was freed, so I named the full disk as the root cause. The memory readings stayed in their normal range throughout, which also points away from a memory problem. A separate failed admin-login attempt on 1 June has nothing to do with the outage.
